identity.name: HAPPY FORGINGS LIMITED

summary.oneLiner: Despite industry headwinds in CV and farm exports, Happy Forgings delivered resilient 3.6% revenue growth and sustained 28.6% EBITDA margin through strong value-addition (88% machining share) and new wins in wind, industrial gensets, and PV segments; the Rs.650cr capacity expansion and Rs.250cr+ new order pipeline position it to capture structural demand in India's energy and EV transition.
summary.business: Happy Forgings is a vertically integrated forging and machining company with capabilities spanning engineering, process design, testing, forging, heat treatment and machining. It serves domestic and global OEMs across the commercial vehicle segment, farm equipment and off-highway vehicles, while participating selectively in industrial sectors such as power generation, wind energy, oil & gas and railways, and has entered the passenger vehicle segment. The portfolio centres on complex, high-precision, value-added forged and machined components including crankshafts up to 250 kg, designed for high-performance and safety-critical reliability.

Forged Components: crankshafts for commercial vehicles, industrial and SUV applications

currentContext.strengths: Vertically integrated capabilities spanning engineering, process design, testing, forging and machining within a unified system, strengthening quality control, cost competitiveness and performance in safety-critical applications|Consciously diversified and flexible business structure enabling response to demand shifts across automotive and industrial segments|Specialised capability to manufacture high-precision, heavy forged components up to 250 kg|Long-standing relationships with 60+ global and domestic OEMs across sectors supporting a balanced, durable customer portfolio|AA/Stable credit ratings from CRISIL and ICRA|Disciplined capital allocation philosophy focused on sustainable margins, healthy cash generation and prudent capital deployment|Seasoned management team and experienced Board providing strategic direction and continuity
currentContext.strategies: Prioritise value-accretive, high-precision, complex components with margin resilience over volume-led growth; capital committed only after evaluating return thresholds, competitive positioning, engineering depth and long-term relevance|Build capacity and capability ahead of visible demand, investing in modern, flexible manufacturing infrastructure designed for scale and adaptability|Calibrated diversification across segments (commercial vehicles, farm equipment, off-highway, industrial - power generation/wind/oil & gas/railways, and passenger vehicles) and geographies, guided by conviction rather than momentum|Continue the shift towards higher value-added, precision-led forged and machined manufacturing - forged and machined products now contribute nearly 89% of revenue versus 73% in 2020-21|Pursue the current large investment programme (including the 10,000-tonne forging press commissioned in the year) to raise scale, complexity and precision for higher-value applications in power generation, energy infrastructure, industrial machinery and data centre ecosystems|Maintain financial prudence and capital efficiency - fund growth through internal accruals, preserve balance sheet resilience and low leverage while continuing to invest|Advance sustainability initiatives including energy efficiency, resource optimisation and captive solar/renewable energy infrastructure as part of long-term competitiveness|Board recommended, subject to shareholder approval at the 47th AGM, a final dividend of Rs 4 per equity share (face value Rs 2) for FY26.
currentContext.expansion: Happy Forgings is executing a Rs 650 Cr. capital expenditure programme, phased over FY2024-25 to FY2026-27, to build advanced forging and machining capabilities for heavyweight components ranging from 250 kg to 3,000 kg - placing it among a select group of global manufacturers with such capability. The new heavy-forging facility is targeted for global sectors including wind energy, oil & gas, marine, defence, nuclear, power generation and farm equipment, and is expected to be commissioned by FY 2026-27 followed by a gradual production ramp-up; at optimal utilisation it is expected to generate Rs 600-800 Cr. in annual revenue. Alongside this, the Company commissioned a 10,000-tonne forging press during FY26 and is also commissioning a 4,000-tonne press to strengthen forging infrastructure and production flexibility. A separate ~Rs 80 Cr. of capital expenditure has been allocated to scale the passenger vehicle segment through dedicated production lines for key SUV platforms. The Company has incurred ~Rs 461 Cr. of capital expenditure in FY 2025-26 against this programme, with investments funded largely through internal accruals to preserve balance-sheet discipline.
currentContext.mdna: Domestic CV industry posted record FY26 sales (10.80 Lakh units, +12.6% YoY); growth expected to normalise to around 5-6% in FY27 per CRISIL, with LCV +5-6%, M&HCV +4-5% and buses +3-4%, supported by infrastructure-led activity and replacement demand|European CV market remained under pressure through CY2025 but showing signs of nearing a cyclical trough into Q1 CY2026; US CV market saw divergence with heavy-duty trucks (Classes 6-8) down ~24% while light-duty (Classes 2-3) grew ~9%|Domestic PV segment achieved record FY26 sales (46.43 Lakh units, +7.9% YoY); growth expected to moderate to 4-6% in FY27 per ICRA, supported by GST benefits and continued utility-vehicle strength|Indian tractor industry saw domestic sales grow 24% YoY in FY26 partly due to pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms; FY27 growth expected to soften to 1-4% amid a high base and below-normal monsoon forecast|Global growth steady but moderated (IMF: 3.1% in 2026, 3.2% in 2027); demand for the forging/machining industry remains linked to capital expenditure cycles in infrastructure, industrial manufacturing and mobility|Supply chain realignment, geoeconomic fragmentation and manufacturing localisation are creating opportunities for cost-efficient, technically capable exporters such as India|Commodity market volatility (energy, metals) and elevated oil prices are flagged as an input-cost and margin risk for forging and machining players|Indian economy expected to remain resilient (FY26 GDP ~7.6%E, RBI projects ~6.9% for FY27), with continued public capex across roads, railways, ports, power and logistics supporting industrial demand

risks.note: Dependence on key customers and specific product segments exposes the Company to fluctuations in demand and industry cycles, and rising input costs may also impact margins; commercial vehicles (37% of revenue) and farm equipment (32%) together account for the bulk of revenue, tying performance to the auto/tractor cycle.
Supply chain disruptions, logistics delays or quality issues may affect production continuity, increase costs and impact customer relationships.

High leverage, interest rate volatility or cash flow mismatches may affect liquidity and investment capacity, making sustained low debt-to-equity and strong internal accruals important to preserve balance-sheet resilience.
Environmental non-compliance or weak ESG performance may result in regulatory penalties, reputational risk or customer attrition.
IT system failures, cyber threats or slow adoption of emerging technologies may affect operations, data security and competitiveness.
Competitive pressure and pricing negotiations from OEMs may impact margins and profitability; regulatory changes may also influence pricing dynamics.

one-line thesis: Despite industry headwinds in CV and farm exports, Happy Forgings delivered resilient 3.6% revenue growth and sustained 28.6% EBITDA margin through strong value-addition (88% machining share) and new wins in wind, industrial gensets, and PV segments; the Rs.650cr capacity expansion and Rs.250cr+ new order pipeline position it to capture structural demand in India's energy and EV transition.
financial scorecard: revenue: +3.6% YoY; EBITDA: +3.6% YoY, margin 28.6% (no distortions); PAT: +3.2% YoY, margin 18.6% (no distortions); order book: Rs.250cr (Europe farm), Rs.300cr (wind), Rs.180cr/yr (industrial gensets), Rs.60cr/yr (wind shafts); net debt: net cash position >Rs.350cr liquidity
guidance: revenue growth: 15-18% medium-term from new businesses; margin: sustain 28%+ EBITDA; order inflow: Rs.250cr+ new wins expected to convert in H2FY26; capex/commissioning: Rs.300cr FY26 (ex-solar), Rs.650cr total capex plan, 10k-ton & 4k-ton presses commissioning by Q2/Q3FY27
order book & pipeline: Rs.250cr (Europe farm OEM), Rs.300cr (wind shafts), Rs.180cr/yr (industrial gensets for data centers), Rs.60cr/yr (wind components), additional PV and defense tenders in pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: CV: 39% rev, -mid single-digit YoY (global weakness); Farm: 32% rev, +high single-digit YoY (India strength, exports negligible); Off-Highway: 10% rev, -mid single-digit (India), -10-12% (EU/US); Industrials: 13% rev, +strong growth (wind, power, O&G); PV: 6% rev, ramping fast, targeting 8-10% of total rev in 2 yrs
growth verticals / optionality: Wind energy (1.2-ton components), industrial gensets (data centers), defense (tender participation), EV front axle beams (35k units FY26), PV suspension components (North America)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 28.6% sustained via 88% machining share, value-addition, and pricing power; raw material price drop of 3% offset by realization stability at Rs.245/kg; fixed cost leverage expected with capacity utilization rise from 59% to 75%+
capex / expansion: Rs.300cr FY26 (ex-solar), Rs.120cr incurred in Q1; Rs.650cr total capex for heavy forging (10k-ton/4k-ton presses, 20k MTPA capacity); Rs.60-70cr solar CPP captive plant (commencing Q1FY27)
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for high-margin segments (wind, industrial, PV); maintaining strong liquidity (>Rs.350cr); no dividend or buyback mentioned; disciplined, value-driven allocation
risks & watch-items: US tariff uncertainty (25-26% on auto components), global CV/farm equipment demand slowdown, delayed infrastructure spending impacting off-highway, execution risk in new capacity ramp-up
management quality / tone: Confident, proactive, and strategically focused; emphasizes diversification, value-addition, and new business wins; dismisses tariff impact as manageable; bullish on medium-term 15-18% growth from new products
non-obvious takeaways: Despite 59% forging utilization, EBITDA margin held via high machining share (88%) and premium product mix; deemed exports flat, but new direct farm exports to Europe are fresh wins, not conversions; PV business is scaling rapidly with new product lines (front steering knuckles, suspension) beyond crankshafts

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
